title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Inline folding replaces a constant name with its value. The guard that keeps it out of comments reads one line at a time, so it knew nothing of a comment block opened above. Inside a KDoc, the prose was treated as code.

highlights.title: KDoc left alone
highlights.description: Measured on a real project: 120 constants qualify for folding and 3 sit inside a comment block, all three in KDoc.

highlights.title: Columns and strings intact
highlights.description: The scan runs on a comment free view that keeps offsets, so decorations land on the same columns and a value used from a string template still folds.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A constant named inside a KDoc block is no longer replaced by its value.
A triple quoted example quoted inside a comment no longer breaks the raw string tracking for the rest of the file.
The extra pass costs 2.2 ms on an 85 KB file and runs once per document version.
